comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Verified on production canary for 48h; no mismatched revision pairs in the autosave audit log.

content.text: Verified on production canary for 48h; no mismatched revision pairs in the autosave audit log.

Editor autosave should always persist the latest document body. On every third successful autosave (approximately every 90 seconds with default debounce), the payload sent to PUT /docs/{id}/revisions contains the body from the previous revision instead of the live editor state.

Expected: each autosave captures the current ProseMirror doc. Actual: saves 1 and 2 are correct; save 3 rewrites the server copy with revision N-1 content, wiping the intervening edits until the next good save.

Cause was a ring buffer of size 2 in AutosaveQueue that rotated the wrong index when flush and enqueue raced after a 2s idle. The third flush reused the stale snapshot reference. Fix re-reads view.state.doc at flush time instead of caching the JSON string at enqueue.
Impact was silent data loss for anyone typing through multiple autosave cycles; several writers reported that their last paragraph vanished after returning from a short break.
